title: Install and configure Drizzle
idea: Drizzle ORM wraps the `pg` driver. You install both, keep the connection string in `DATABASE_URL`, and export one `db` object that every query uses.

analogy.text: A switchboard. `DATABASE_URL` is the number to dial, the pool is a bank of open lines, and `db` is the one desk every call goes through.
analogy.breaks: A real pool has a limit: extra queries wait for a free connection.

points: `DATABASE_URL` in `.env` holds one connection string: user, password, host, port, database.
`drizzle(url)` creates a `pg` pool, a set of reusable connections, and returns `db`.
`drizzle-kit`, a command-line tool, reads `drizzle.config.js` for the schema path and database.

parts.label: Scheme
parts.note: Names the kind of database. PostgreSQL accepts `postgres://` or `postgresql://`.

parts.label: User
parts.note: The database role to log in as. The Docker image creates `postgres` by default.

parts.label: Password
parts.note: Set by `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`. A demo value: never commit a real one.

parts.label: Host
parts.note: Where the database runs. `localhost` is your own machine.

parts.label: Port
parts.note: Postgres listens on 5432 by default. With `-p 127.0.0.1:5433:5432`, use 5433.

parts.label: Database
parts.note: Which database on the server. The image names it after the user.

code.caption: Run in the project folder. `-D` saves `drizzle-kit` as a dev dependency. The password is a demo value.

code.title: drizzle.config.js
code.caption: Read by the `drizzle-kit` command line, never by your app. Shown here, not run.

walk.text: Load `.env`, so `process.env.DATABASE_URL` exists when `drizzle-kit` reads this file.
`dialect` names the database; `schema` points at the file with your tables.
`out` is the folder for migration files.
`dbCredentials.url` is the connection string `drizzle-kit` connects with.

pitfalls: Add `.env` to `.gitignore`: it holds your password and must never be committed.
Check `DATABASE_URL` at startup: `drizzle(undefined)` fails only at the first query.
In scripts, call `db.$client.end()`; otherwise the process waits for idle connections to time out.

quiz.why: The port follows the host. The path after the slash is the database name; `slice(1)` drops the leading `/`.

takeaway: Read `DATABASE_URL` once, build `db` once, import it everywhere.
